conventions.convention: The laboratory chart is positively oriented, x⁰=ct, dt=dx⁰/c, with spatial volume dx¹∧dx²∧dx³. F=B-form−dt∧E-form, G=D-form+dt∧H-form, and the free-current form is ρ_f vol₃−dt∧J_sp.
The Hodge star uses signature (−+++), orientation dx⁰∧dx¹∧dx²∧dx³, and satisfies star²=−id on two-forms; star(dx²∧dx³)=dx⁰∧dx¹.
Continuous-form integrals use the fixed positive affine coordinates on standard simplices and finite real chain coefficients. Degenerate simplex maps are permitted; the zero chain has integral zero.

The exterior Maxwell equivalence assumes jointly C¹ E,B and C² P,M; classical free-current closure additionally assumes C² E,B. Flux constancy concerns a fixed finite smooth singular spatial two-cycle over a nonempty open time interval.
The duality angle is a constant real number. The symmetry concerns source-free vacuum equations and does not assert preservation of material closure or boundary conditions.
The tetrahedron vertices have the displayed order and determinant −16a³, so the outward radial cycle uses coefficients (−1)^(i+1). The origin is excluded, Φ is nonzero with units Wb, and a=1 m.
The PEC boundary model used in the example imposes exactly E_parallel=E−(E·n)n=0 on x₃=0, using continuous traces and n=(0,0,1).

load_bearing.statement: For jointly C¹ E,B, jointly C² P,M, and the adopted smooth vacuum Maxwell equations on I×Ω, dF=0 and dG=𝒥 are equivalent to div B=0, curl E=−∂tB, div D=ρ_f, and curl H=J_f+∂tD. These equations follow without a material constitutive law. Where P=M=0, G=(μ₀c)⁻¹ star F and star²=−id on two-forms. With C² E,B,P,M, d𝒥=0, equivalently ∂tρ_f+div J_f=0. Magnetic flux through any fixed finite real smooth singular spatial two-cycle is constant on I.

In the fixed oriented SI laboratory chart, F=𝓑−dt∧𝓔, G=𝓓+dt∧𝓗, and 𝒥=ρ_f vol₃−dt∧𝓙_sp. The definition specifies the coordinate exterior derivative for C¹ forms and cycle flux by continuous-form chain integrals; it imposes no constitutive relation.

For an open V⊆Rⁿ, 1≤k≤n, a continuous k-form ω, and a smooth singular simplex σ:Δᵏ→V, define its integral as the Riemann integral of the continuous pullback coefficient in fixed positive affine coordinates; extend by finite real linear sums to smooth singular chains. These integrals exist and agree with the smooth-form convention.

Let T={u∈R³:u_i≥0, u₁+u₂+u₃≤1} have positive affine orientation and signed outward boundary. For η=f₁du²∧du³−f₂du¹∧du³+f₃du¹∧du² of class C¹ on a neighbourhood of T, with dη=(∂₁f₁+∂₂f₂+∂₃f₃)du¹∧du²∧du³, the continuous-form integrals satisfy integral_T dη=integral_boundary-T η.

For a C¹ vacuum field-strength two-form with P=M=0 and 𝒥=0, and constant real θ, Fθ=cos(θ)F+sin(θ)star F again satisfies dFθ=0 and d star Fθ=0. With nonzero free current and sin(θ)≠0, the same no-magnetic-source equation generally fails; no material or boundary invariance is asserted.

concerns.concern: The summary says, “The cycle has no global smooth potential”. The proved obstruction belongs to the field-strength two-form F, not to the cycle z. The example itself states the correct conclusion; the page sentence should identify the field-strength form as the object without a global smooth potential.

seams_checked.note: Checked the supplier page and its Hodge-star definition and square lemma against the consumer definitions and vacuum-closure/duality calculations. Orientation, signature, basis signs, and degree-two square agree. The consumer establishes its C¹ integration and Stokes extension locally rather than attributing that regularity to smooth-only suppliers.

Checked both consumer uses against the supplier statements and proofs: the outward sphere integral is 4π, the obstruction requires a genuine finite smooth cycle and a smooth closed two-form with nonzero period, and star(dx²∧dx³)=dx⁰∧dx¹ gives Eθ=−cB at the quarter-turn. The radial cycle construction meets the hypotheses. The page's cycle-versus-form wording defect is recorded separately.
